key_points: The Seattle Times and Newsday sued OpenAI and Microsoft over alleged copyright infringement related to AI training.
The lawsuit claims generative AI acts as a 'snake eating its own tail' by consuming and imitating human-authored content.
This case follows a 2023 lawsuit filed by The New York Times against OpenAI and Microsoft.
Microsoft and OpenAI have funded some of The Seattle Times' journalism projects despite the legal dispute.
A Microsoft spokesperson said the company is surprised by the lawsuit but willing to explore solutions.
items.summary: The Seattle Times and Newsday filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft, alleging the companies used their journalism to train generative AI models. The plaintiffs argue that AI systems consume human content to produce derivative imitations, potentially breaking the journalism industry. This action follows a 2023 suit by The New York Times against the same defendants. Notably, Microsoft and OpenAI have previously funded some of The Seattle Times' journalism projects. A Microsoft spokesperson expressed surprise at the filing but stated the company is open to exploring solutions.
items.title: Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft over AI training

It excels at building sophisticated 3D models, creating renderings of gardens, shipyards, and cityscapes. The blog notes the model can produce complex outputs like Dyson spheres.

key_points: Daily crude oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have fallen to between 6 and 8 million barrels.
The global energy import bill increased by $330 billion from March to August due to rising prices.
Japan recorded a record oil import bill of $76.39 billion in July as it sought alternative suppliers.
The conflict is creating a more expensive global oil network less reliant on critical waterways.
items.summary: The ongoing conflict in the Middle East is driving a permanent restructuring of global oil and gas trade routes. Oil exporters are urgently diversifying channels away from the Strait of Hormuz, while importers scramble to find alternative suppliers. The article reports that daily crude flows through the strait have dropped from 20 million barrels to between 6 and 8 million barrels. Nations like Saudi Arabia and the UAE are redirecting shipments to ports such as Yanbu and Fujairah, though capacity constraints remain a significant hurdle. Import costs have surged, with the global energy import bill swelling by $330 billion between March and August. Japan now relies on distant suppliers like the US and Canada, leading to record import bills. The transformation creates a more expensive, less centralized network less vulnerable to single-point failures.
items.title: Iran War Forces Global Oil Trade Route Rewrites

key_points: Japan and South Korea are reviving their nuclear energy sectors to prioritize baseload clean energy.
The United States is partnering with these nations to secure reactor technology supply chains in the region.
The three countries signed a cooperation agreement in July to deploy small-scale modular reactors.
The alliance aims to provide competitive alternatives to Chinese and Russian nuclear vendors.
items.summary: Japan, South Korea, and the United States are forming a new trilateral nuclear alliance to reshape energy security in Northeast Asia. The Diplomat reported that this cooperation integrates energy policy into broader security strategies, offering strategic benefits to all three nations. The Foreign Policy Journal noted that Washington has an interest in ensuring its allies become default suppliers of reactor technology rather than China or Russia. Haley Zaremba for Oilprice.com wrote that the alliance aims to limit the influence of rival powers in regional energy markets. The three countries signed a cooperation agreement in July for the deployment of small-scale modular reactors. The U.S. Department of State stated the memorandum outlines opportunities for mutually beneficial cooperation among their respective nuclear industries. This framework aims to foster fleet deployment models that de-risk project development and optimize supply chains.
items.title: Japan, South Korea and the U.S. Forge a New Nuclear Alliance

key_points: The Volkswagen Supervisory Board unanimously approved CEO Oliver Blume's restructuring plan on September 3, 2026.
The approved strategy targets a total workforce reduction of 100,000 employees and the elimination of half of the company's current vehicle models.
While the plan confirms the need to address excess European capacity, it leaves the specific fate of four German factories undecided until a new production structure is developed by June 2027.
Union leaders stated that while the confrontational approach was unconstructive, the decision prevents immediate plant closures and protects co-determination structures.
items.summary: The Volkswagen Supervisory Board unanimously approved CEO Oliver Blume's restructuring plan on September 3, 2026, following an initial rejection in July. The approved strategy targets a total workforce reduction of 100,000 employees and the elimination of half of the company's current vehicle models. While the plan confirms the need to address excess European capacity, it leaves the specific fate of four German factories undecided until a new production structure is developed by June 2027. Union leaders stated that while the confrontational approach was unconstructive, the decision prevents immediate plant closures and protects co-determination structures. The article notes that despite these measures, Volkswagen faces significant challenges including rising tariffs in the US, declining sales in China, and a shifting market toward electric vehicles.
items.title: Volkswagen Supervisory Board Approves Plan To Slash Models And Reduce Workforce By 100,000

key_points: A University of Swansea study found that 86% of licensed British gambling websites appear to be flouting GDPR rules.
Nearly a quarter of the tested sites did not offer users the option to turn off tracking software.
Two-thirds of operators began harvesting user data before receiving consent for collection.
Researchers noted that 86% of sites using 'dark patterns' also committed at least one GDPR breach.
The Information Commissioner's Office stated it is committed to monitoring compliance and taking action where necessary.
items.summary: A study by researchers at the University of Swansea's GREAT Centre accuses nearly 90% of licensed British gambling websites of violating GDPR rules regarding cookie banners. The research found that 86% of the sites tested failed to comply with strict data protection regulations. Approximately 24% of the 624 gambling websites examined did not provide users the option to disable tracking software, while two-thirds began harvesting data before obtaining consent. The report highlights that operators frequently use 'dark patterns' to nudge users toward accepting data sharing. Ravi Naik of AWO described the findings as evidence of systemic non-compliance and criticized the Information Commissioner's Office for a lack of meaningful enforcement. While the ICO stated it remains committed to monitoring compliance, several major operators declined to comment on the specific allegations.
items.title: Study accuses UK online bookies of widespread GDPR privacy breaches

Customers have largely embraced this new local alternative.

key_points: Recent severe weather in the UK caused significant flight delays and cancellations, highlighting growing climate risks for aviation.
Experts warn that simultaneous airport closures due to storms could create serious safety risks for passengers and crews.
Clear-air turbulence is becoming more prevalent, with incidents over the North Atlantic increasing by 55% since 1979.
Rising sea levels threaten hundreds of coastal airports globally, potentially costing billions in flood defenses and relocation.
The aviation industry must balance carbon neutrality goals with adapting to a climate that will cause more frequent disruptions.
items.summary: Aviation faces increasing disruption from hotter, stormier skies as climate change intensifies weather systems globally. The article reports that recent severe weather in the UK caused hundreds of flight delays and cancellations, prompting industry warnings about future instability. Experts like Tim Atkinson caution that crowded skies could lead to simultaneous airport closures, creating serious risks for passengers and crews. While some industry figures like Andrew Charlton believe worst-case scenarios remain unlikely, others note that more intense storms will likely increase fuel costs and delay times. Clear-air turbulence is also becoming more prevalent, with incidents rising significantly since 1979. Additionally, rising sea levels threaten coastal airports, with hundreds of facilities globally at risk of flooding. The aviation industry faces a dual challenge of meeting carbon neutrality targets while adapting to a changing climate that will inevitably cause more disagreeable moments for travelers.
items.title: Aviation faces hotter skies and stormier weather as climate change mounts

key_points: A scientific collaboration between Australian researchers and Bardi Jawi rangers identified migration patterns of culturally important fish between reefs and mangroves.
Phillip "Bibido" McCarthy stated that the study confirmed traditional knowledge that both ecosystems are essential for fish survival against climate change.
Katherine Cure explained that Indigenous knowledge provides a holistic view of connected ecosystems that Western science often misses.
The research findings directly influenced the zoning and design of the Bardi Jawi Indigenous Protected Area and the Bardi Jawi Gaarra Marine Park.
items.summary: A collaboration between Australian scientists and Bardi Jawi rangers found that culturally important fish species migrate between reefs and mangroves in the Kimberley region. The study, published in Ocean & Coastal Management, confirmed traditional ecological knowledge while adding scientific metrics on species abundance. Phillip "Bibido" McCarthy noted that without healthy mangroves or reefs, certain fish may not survive climate threats. Katherine Cure, a lead author, explained that Western science often compartmentalizes ecosystems, whereas Indigenous knowledge views them as interconnected systems. The partnership allowed scientists to use long-term traditional data alongside modern technology like drones. Findings guided the design of the Bardi Jawi Indigenous Protected Area and marine park. Both parties learned that ecosystem resilience depends on the health of both habitats.
items.title: Indigenous knowledge reveals reef-mangrove ties for fish survival

The Lawn Tennis Association stated most displaced courts were underutilised or in poor condition.

Tennis courts still outnumber padel courts by a factor of 11 to one despite the recent surge.

The Lawn Tennis Association states most displaced courts were underutilised or in poor condition. Padel participation reached one million players by May, driven by smaller court sizes and accessibility. Despite the rise, tennis courts still outnumber padel courts by a factor of 11 to one.
items.title: England loses 183 tennis courts as padel facilities surge

The car driver was not physically injured, and police are investigating the crash.

Emergency services responded to Horseshoe Bay just before 12pm, where bystanders and lifeguards attempted resuscitation efforts. The car driver sustained no physical injuries, though police could not confirm if the deceased was a tourist. A forensic crash unit is currently investigating the incident.
items.title: Canadian woman dies after moped crash on Magnetic Island

Jon Barker leads the NFL's global event operations and production team for this debut.

key_points: Doctors Without Borders states that mortality rates for children under five during the Ebola outbreak exceed 60%.
Current experimental antiviral studies often exclude children weighing less than 30 kilograms, limiting their access to treatment.
Pediatric experts explain that children metabolize drugs differently, necessitating separate studies to determine safe dosages.
Marc Biot of Doctors Without Borders argues that pharmaceutical companies prioritize adult trials to save costs, delaying pediatric access.
Neal Russell calls for sub-studies to include children and pregnant women from the outset of clinical trials during health emergencies.
items.summary: Doctors Without Borders argues that young children must be centered in Ebola treatment and prevention research. The organization highlights that mortality rates for children under five exceed 60% due to medication gaps rather than the disease itself. Current studies often exclude children under 30 kilograms, leaving them without access to experimental antivirals like obeldesivir. Pediatric experts explain that children metabolize drugs differently, requiring separate studies to determine safe dosages and formulations. Marc Biot of Doctors Without Borders notes that pharmaceutical companies often prioritize adult trials to save costs, delaying pediatric access. Neal Russell emphasizes that during health emergencies, the balance between research safety and disease protection must shift to include vulnerable groups immediately. The article concludes by calling for sub-studies to include children and pregnant women from the outset of clinical trials.
items.title: Doctors Without Borders calls for children to be prioritized in Ebola treatment research

key_points: Iran said its forces attacked a U.S. naval drone trying to enter the Strait of Hormuz.
The attack happened hours after Iran targeted ships in retaliation for American strikes on three oil tankers.
The latest round of clashes began with U.S. raids last week.
Iran maintains control of the Strait of Hormuz while Washington continues a counterblockade of Iranian ports.
items.summary: Iran announced on Sunday that its forces struck a U.S. naval drone attempting to enter the Strait of Hormuz. This action occurred hours after Iran targeted ships in response to American strikes on three oil tankers. The recent clashes mark the latest escalation in their ongoing six-month conflict. Iran continues to control the strategic Strait of Hormuz while the United States maintains a counterblockade of Iranian ports.
items.title: Iran attacks U.S. drone after striking oil tankers

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reaffirmed Kyiv's readiness to pause strikes during the envoys' visit.
Putin ordered Russian forces to halt strikes on Kyiv for three days while the envoys are in Ukraine.

Osaka apologized to children watching the match after she threw her racquet to the floor.
The player described her Achilles problem as an ongoing issue that has persisted since the grass season.
Osaka will face No. 2 seed Elena Rybakina in the upcoming round of the tournament.

She will face No. 2 seed Elena Rybakina in the next round.
items.title: Naomi Osaka apologizes to children after US Open upset

key_points: Hungary's new government plans to recover billions of euros allegedly stolen by the previous Orban regime.
The National Asset Recovery Authority has been created with broad powers to investigate and prosecute corruption cases.
Anna Unger was appointed to head the new agency despite not being a lawyer, a decision that surprised many experts.
The head of the authority warned that legally binding verdicts in major corruption cases might not happen within the agency's first six years.
items.summary: Hungary's new government has initiated a major campaign to recover billions of euros allegedly misappropriated by the previous administration. Prime Minister Peter Magyar and his Tisza party aim to retrieve funds sent to Viktor Orban's allies and hold them legally accountable. The state established the National Asset Recovery Authority, a powerful new body with policing and prosecutorial powers to investigate public fund usage since 2010. Anna Unger was appointed to lead the agency, though her lack of legal background sparked controversy among observers. While the authority investigates past corruption, its head stated that legally binding verdicts in major cases may not occur within its first six-year term, a claim that drew sharp criticism from political commentators.
items.title: Hungary launches asset recovery hunt for billions linked to ousted Orban regime

The Big Ten confirmed the review and provided video evidence supporting the ruling.

The Big Ten confirmed the review, citing a rule that stops the clock on out-of-bounds contact. Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham described the narrow escape as avoiding an 'epic loss' before facing No. 10 Oklahoma next week.
items.title: Michigan survives disputed replay to beat Western Michigan 13-12

key_points: The AfD party aims to become the first far-right group to take state power in Germany since World War II.
German intelligence agencies classify the party as right-wing extremist due to its connections with ethno-nationalist groups.
An absolute majority would allow the AfD to govern alone, but the party may struggle to form a coalition if it falls short.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz hopes the election will reduce the AfD's popularity through his tougher stance on migration.
items.summary: Germany's far-right AfD party is targeting a historic win in the Saxony-Anhalt state election, potentially becoming the first such party to govern since World War II. The party, led by Ulrich Siegmund, currently polls at over 40 percent but faces the challenge of securing an absolute majority to bypass Germany's "firewall" policy. Domestic intelligence agencies classify the party as right-wing extremist due to its links to ethno-nationalist groups and past meetings discussing radical remigration plans. If the AfD fails to win a majority, a CDU-led administration under Sven Schulze is the most likely outcome, though complex coalition negotiations may follow. The election serves as a barometer for Chancellor Friedrich Merz's government and reflects lingering economic resentment in eastern Germany.
items.title: AfD aims historic state victory in Saxony-Anhalt election

Global food prices have risen to their highest level in nearly four years due to Black Sea disruptions. Additionally, a local ceasefire was brokered by the IAEA to restore power to the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant.
items.title: Trump envoys visit Moscow for peace talks amid Ukraine war updates

key_points: Researchers successfully extracted ancient DNA from antelope fossils in South Africa.
The oldest DNA found belonged to a mountain reedbuck at Boomplaas Cave.
Most fossils with preserved DNA were younger than 11,700 years old.
Collagen preservation correlates with DNA preservation at 77% of sites.
The study enables genetic analysis of African mammals extinct after the last ice age.
items.summary: Researchers report that they successfully extracted ancient DNA from antelope fossils in South Africa, opening a new window into the region's past. The team tested 144 fossils aged 1,500 to 110,000 years and found DNA preserved for up to 50,000 years, though most samples were younger than 11,700 years. They identified the oldest DNA as belonging to a mountain reedbuck at Boomplaas Cave, potentially 30,000 years old. The study shows that African large mammals can be genetically studied despite warmer climates that usually degrade DNA. The authors note that only about 2% of extracted DNA came from the target species on average. They also found a 77% correlation between collagen preservation and DNA preservation, suggesting collagen can serve as a proxy for selecting fossils for sequencing.
items.title: Researchers recover ancient antelope DNA from South African fossils

items.summary: An economist argues that Africa receives only 23% of the climate finance it requires to meet its Paris Agreement commitments. The author states that vulnerable nations receive merely 11% of continental funding while ten other countries attract 76% of private investment. Current financing covers just 18% of planned mitigation projects and 20% of adaptation costs. The speaker notes that renewable energy projects cost two to three times more in Africa than in advanced economies due to higher borrowing costs. The article concludes that African diplomacy must shift from seeking labeled climate finance to building local industries and manufacturing capabilities.
items.title: Economist argues Africa receives only 23% of needed climate finance

key_points: Lane Kiffin led No. 11 LSU to a 51-10 victory over Clemson in his first game as head coach.
Quarterback Sam Leavitt recorded 230 passing yards and 113 rushing yards with two touchdowns.
LSU accumulated 644 total yards of offense while Clemson suffered its worst loss in about 30 years.
A lightning delay pushed the start of the game back nearly two hours at Tiger Stadium.
items.summary: Lane Kiffin guided No. 11 LSU to a 51-10 victory over Clemson in his debut as the program's head coach. Quarterback Sam Leavitt threw for 230 yards and a touchdown while rushing for 113 yards and two scores. Edge rusher Jordan Ross returned an interception for a touchdown, contributing to the team's dominant performance. The win came despite a two-hour delay caused by lightning and rain at Tiger Stadium. LSU finished with 644 total yards of offense, handing Clemson its worst loss in roughly 30 years. Clemson coach Dabo Swinney attributed the defeat to a poor defensive performance against the run. LSU rushed for 213 yards in the first half alone, a significant improvement from the previous season. The victory marks a strong start for Kiffin and athletic director Verge Ausberry.
items.title: Lane Kiffin leads No. 11 LSU to a 51-10 victory over Clemson

The match lasted 9 hours and 26 minutes after Zverev played five previous sets against Sonego and Halys.

items.summary: Residents and activists in Chuburná Puerto, Yucatán, are protesting a luxury real estate project built atop endangered coastal dunes. Karen Sosa, a local native, stated that developers view the coast as vacant land, ignoring the thriving ecosystem that supports endangered species like the Mexican sheartail. On July 31, demonstrators demanded the permanent halt of the Dunas Tourist Complex and the revocation of its permits. The Federal Attorney for Environmental Protection (PROFEPA) temporarily shut down the project on July 30 due to violations causing irreversible damage to the ecosystem. Gabriela Mendoza warned that such developments destroy natural buffers against climate change. The project, by Designia Desarrollos, plans 138 apartments on 99,000 square feet of land, despite municipal plans designating the area as non-developable. Economist Javier Becerril noted that these high-value properties cater to foreign retirees, creating social exclusion for local residents who earn significantly less than the average apartment price.

items.summary: Museum robberies have surged since 2023 as rising gold prices motivate violent gangs to target historical artifacts. Recent thefts in Villena, Badajoz, and Albacete, Spain, involved priceless collections worth millions when melted down. Experts note that the black market for stolen gold is poorly regulated, facilitating the sale of illicit artifacts. The Spanish Ministry of Culture has since requested museums report gold holdings and reinforced security protocols. Similar incidents, including a 2025 Louvre heist, highlight the growing threat to cultural heritage.
items.title: Rising Gold Prices Fuel Museum Robberies Across Europe

items.summary: An author documents Tharu oral culture in eastern Nepal to reveal untold facets of Indigenous stories. The work involves spending time with communities to record folktales, songs, and personal experiences. The author shares findings from a folk song called Morangsair, which details seasonal migration patterns and historical river geography. Research indicates the Koshi River once flowed further east, while a river named Biyahi is actually named after the Tharu word for a married woman. Additionally, interviews with elderly women revealed that traditional sago pearls were made from palm tree pith, a practice now rare. The author expresses a desire to share these stories with a wider audience after losing their grandmother, who originally told them.
items.title: Author documents Tharu folklore to uncover overlooked Indigenous stories

items.summary: Google has reportedly confirmed its planned 1-GW data centre in Visakhapatnam will use air-cooling technology following local protests. A 1-GW centre generates immense heat that air-cooling alone cannot efficiently remove without incurring high energy costs and noise pollution. Experts note that modern AI chips generate heat densities far exceeding the 40 kW per rack limit of standard air-cooling systems. Consequently, many large facilities now employ hybrid cooling methods combining air and liquid systems. Google also pledged to replenish 120% of its non-cooling water consumption by 2030. Meanwhile, TCS announced its HyperVault facility will utilize direct-to-chip liquid cooling for high-density AI operations.
items.title: Google adopts air-cooling for Visakhapatnam data centre despite physics limits

items.summary: Google has launched an artificial intelligence project in India to enhance agricultural productivity and climate resilience. Alok Talekar, Lead of Agriculture and Sustainability Research at Google DeepMind, stated the initiative aims to responsibly transform the lives of millions of farmers. The project utilizes two AI models, Agricultural Landscape Understanding and Agricultural Monitoring and Event Detection, to map fields and track activity via satellite imagery. Google has established the AnthroKrishi team to organize global agricultural information and make it accessible through APIs and Google Earth. The models have been shared with trusted testers in 11 countries across Asia-Pacific and Africa. Google is collaborating with state governments in Karnataka and Telangana to integrate these tools for water management and crop advisories. Partners like CarbonFarm are using the technology to automate field insights and support carbon credit programs. Google has also partnered with the UN's Food and Agriculture Organisation to integrate these models into global data repositories. Talekar noted that the current system primarily looks backwards at historical data to provide transparent information for downstream applications.
items.title: Google launches AI project to boost farm productivity and climate resilience

items.summary: India voted in favor of a United Nations resolution to adopt an equal-area world map, emphasizing the principle of fair cartographic representation. While several political parties condemned the behavior, the author criticizes the VLEN coalition and VMRO-DPMNE for failing to directly name or dismiss the officials responsible. Jashari warns that tolerating such views contradicts North Macedonia's commitment to European values and hinders its integration into the European Union. The article concludes that a state cannot build a European future while allowing the glorification of convicted war criminals.
items.title: Author argues North Macedonia must stop glorifying convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić

items.summary: Director Honey Trehan discussed the challenges faced by his film Satluj, which depicts the life of human rights defender Jaswant Singh Khalra. Trehan stated that the movie was blocked by the government's censor board for 31 years before its eventual release on an OTT platform. He attributed the film's widespread popularity to unauthorized screenings and piracy, noting it achieved a 9.7 rating on IMDb within days. Trehan argued that political motives drove narratives claiming the film incited violence, asserting Khalra fought for all undocumented victims regardless of religion. The director emphasized that the film united diverse communities in Punjab and provided emotional healing to those affected by past political violence. Trehan rejected accusations that the film glorifies violence, explaining it portrays a specific historical period rather than being a biopic. He criticized the selective application of national security threats, contrasting Satluj with other controversial films that received awards. Trehan confirmed his producer, Ronnie Screwvala, lost crores of rupees due to pressure to make cuts that were never implemented. The director expressed pride in the project, viewing it as a service to his community and humanity.
items.title: Director Honey Trehan Defends Film Satluj Against Government Censorship

key_points: Jing-Jing Lee's novel How We Disappeared focuses on the experiences of Wang Di, a young girl forced into sexual slavery during the Japanese occupation of Singapore.
The Japanese occupation began in February 1942 and resulted in the deaths of roughly 55,000 ethnic Chinese while young women were trafficked as comfort women.
After the war, survivors faced intense ostracization from their families and communities, struggling to reintegrate into society.
The Japanese government has denied operating state-sponsored rape camps, though victims from South Korea, the Philippines, Taiwan, and Indonesia continue to demand acknowledgment.
Lee's story is inspired by her own family history, highlighting the enduring impact of these historical traumas on subsequent generations.
items.summary: Jing-Jing Lee's 2019 novel How We Disappeared centers on Wang Di, a young girl trafficked as a comfort woman during Japan's occupation of Singapore. The article notes that the Japanese military occupied Singapore in February 1942, claiming the lives of approximately 55,000 ethnic Chinese and kidnapping young women for the army. Lee's protagonist survives in a brothel where she serves up to 50 men daily while suffering from venereal diseases and facing constant threats. After the war, the novel depicts the severe ostracization these women faced upon returning to their families. The Japanese government has denied running state-sponsored rape camps, yet victims from multiple nations continue to seek justice. Lee's work keeps these memories alive, ensuring the suffering of these women is not forgotten.
items.title: Jing-Jing Lee's novel honors comfort women of occupied Singapore

items.summary: The Times of India explains how Indian inheritance laws differ across religious communities and property types. Hindu women gain equal coparcenary rights by birth under the 2005 amendment, clarified by the Supreme Court in 2020. Muslim inheritance depends on family structure and applicable personal law, while Christian and Parsi succession follows the Indian Succession Act with equal treatment for sons and daughters. Advocates note that self-acquired property can be excluded from a daughter via will, but existing coparcenary shares cannot be extinguished. The article outlines legal steps to challenge unfair wills and warns against informal relinquishment of rights under family pressure.
items.title: Indian inheritance laws vary by religion and property type for women

key_points: Researchers followed nearly 3,000 Swedish adults aged 60 and over to examine the effects of long gaps between meals.
Participants who habitually went 14 to 24 hours without eating developed chronic diseases faster than those with shorter fasting periods.
The link between long fasting and faster disease accumulation was strongest among people aged 78 and over.
The authors note that this was an observational study, so they cannot determine if fasting caused the disease or if poor health led to longer fasting.
items.summary: A study of nearly 3,000 Swedish adults aged 60 and over found that longer gaps between meals were linked to faster development of chronic diseases. The researchers, led by Adrián Carballo Casla at Karolinska Institutet, observed that this association was clearest among participants aged 78 and over. While fasting benefits younger adults by improving metabolism, older bodies may struggle with nutrient absorption and muscle maintenance during long fasting periods. The study tracked diagnoses of 60 chronic diseases over up to 15 years, noting faster accumulation of conditions like heart failure and dementia in those with longer fasting times. However, the authors caution that this was an observational study, meaning they cannot confirm that fasting caused the disease progression rather than poor health leading to longer fasting periods.
items.title: Study finds long gaps between meals affect older adults differently
